review_notes:
I read the whole file. Its only definitions are T2Aux.resEquiv, T2Aux.ev and T2Aux.compVal. The rest is auxiliary lemmas and the main theorem `solution`.

- resEquiv is `RingEquiv.ofBijective` applied to the algebra map into the residue field. That is the standard Mathlib construction, so it is not a competing concept.
- ev composes the inverse of resEquiv with the residue map. It is a thin local helper, and I found no Mathlib counterpart.
- compVal builds the valuation subring of F whose elements lie in P's valuation ring and whose evaluation at P lands in A. This is a composite valuation ring. A grep of Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation for composite or residue-comap constructions returned nothing, so I found no existing Mathlib definition of it.

The unit, nonunit and comap helper lemmas (inv_mem_of_isUnit, mem_nonunits_comap_iff and similar) are standalone theorem duplication at most, and the rubric excludes that. I did not check how `Place.evalAt` or the `Place` API in the project's own definition files relate to Mathlib, because that is a project API and not Mathlib.

I found no justified duplicate-concept finding. My search of Mathlib was brief, so some uncertainty remains.
